briefs.source_chain: Momentum basket selloff exceeds desk's own summer-slump forecast, therefore hyperscaler/data-center-equipment valuations and positioning sit near multi-year/liberation-day lows with low correlation to momentum, therefore desk recommends buying the dip in both baskets ahead of an earnings season following MU/Samsung beats and META's cloud launch.
briefs.brief_chain: Momentum selloff exceeds the desk's own summer-slump expectation, therefore hyperscaler and data-center valuations and positioning are near multi-year lows with low correlation to momentum, therefore buying the dip is cheap and balances momentum exposure, framed ahead of earnings season following MU/Samsung beats and META's cloud launch.

distortions.what: Brief drops the source's added comparison that hyperscaler cheapness is 'similar to liberation day lows as well as US-Iran war peak' — only liberation-day framing is kept.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the valuation-cheapness point and the buy-the-dip call are unaffected by dropping one of two historical reference points.

distortions.what: Brief's valuation survey omits the Memory (GSTMTMEM) sub-basket the source lists as its own category.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — source gives no directional read or numbers for Memory beyond naming it, so nothing actionable is lost.

briefs.source_chain: Sustained earnings growth keeps GS OW equities/UW credit for 12m, but with returns slowing and elevated risk appetite, upside now needs lower rates, therefore stay invested/buy dips/hedge; overnight, GS turns buyer of AVGO on FY27-28 AI revenue guidance and custom-silicon breadth, expects HPE to trade lower on already-elevated expectations despite a beat, and expects CRDO to trade lower near-term on elevated expectations while remaining Buy-rated on favorable risk/reward.
briefs.brief_chain: GS stays OW equities/UW credit into 12m as earnings growth slows and further upside needs lower rates, therefore stay invested and buy dips; overnight GS turns buyer of AVGO on FY27/FY28 AI revenue guidance, and expects both HPE and CRDO to trade modestly lower despite solid quarters, against elevated expectations.

distortions.what: Brief says GS 'expects both [HPE and CRDO] to trade modestly lower' with no further qualifier, dropping the source's explicit 'We remain Buy-rated on CRDO ... favorable risk/reward for the stock at current levels.' HPE carries no such rating statement in the source, so the omission lands only on CRDO.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — read alone, the brief's line reads as a near-term-bearish/avoid signal on CRDO, whereas GS's actual stance is a maintained Buy with favorable risk-reward through the dip; a trader acting on the brief could skip or short a name GS is telling clients to hold/buy.

distortions.what: Brief keeps 'Anthropic largest FY27 custom silicon customer' but drops the source's further detail that GS expects OpenAI and Meta to be material FY28 customers.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the AVGO buy call and its rationale (revenue doubling, Anthropic as top FY27 customer, secured supply) are unaffected by dropping a forward-looking secondary customer note.

distortions.what: Brief compresses 'stay invested, buying dips and mitigating risk through diversification and selective overlay hedges' to 'buy dips and hedge selectively', dropping the diversification clause.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the actionable stance (stay invested, buy dips, hedge) is preserved.

distortions.what: Brief omits the Market Update paragraph (SPX/NDX/RTY closing levels, sector breadth) entirely.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — this is scene-setting market recap, not part of any call or forecast in the brief.

briefs.source_chain: Rates relief and stabilizing momentum lifted US small caps while Europe fell a third session on an autos/cyclicals energy-and-rates squeeze, therefore GS stays tactically neutral 3m/modestly pro-risk 12m and buys dips while hedging seasonal and election risk (French Domestic basket), and separately flags a 5mb/d upward revision to Persian Gulf oil exports from AIS-off tanker crossings, plus single-name Buy calls on Broadcom (target raised to $540), Auto1, PPC and Ferrari.
briefs.brief_chain: Rates relief lifted US small caps while Europe fell a third session on an energy/rates squeeze on autos and cyclicals, therefore GS stays tactically neutral 3m/pro-risk 12m, buys dips, and hedges election risk via the French Domestic basket; separately, dark tanker crossings near Oman imply Gulf oil exports well above visible flows, and GS carries Buy ratings with raised targets on Auto1, PPC and Ferrari after in-line Broadcom results.

distortions.what: Brief states GS carries 'raised targets' on Ferrari alongside Auto1 and PPC, but the source shows explicit target increases only for Auto1 (EUR37 from EUR36.5) and PPC (EUR27 from EUR26.5); Ferrari's PT (EUR407) is stated with no '(from ...)' prior-target marker indicating a change.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — Ferrari's rating (Buy) and the actionable call are unchanged either way; only the 'raised' framing is unsupported by the source text.

distortions.what: Brief drops the source's framing that estimated Gulf exports (15-16mb/d) are 'roughly 2/3 of pre-war levels'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the core figures (15-16mb/d vs 10mb/d visible, 5mb/d revision, AIS-off cause) are all retained.

distortions.what: Brief drops Broadcom's prior target ($525) and gross-margin beat detail (75.0% vs 74.1% cons).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the target level ($540) and in-line-revenue/guidance-just-below-Street characterization are preserved.

briefs.source_chain: Dovish Waller comments (doubt on a Sept hike, disinflation signs) plus falling European natgas paused the bond selloff and drove a cross-asset rally, therefore equities (SPX +1.06%) outperformed a mostly front-end-led Treasury rally, even as hawkish data (ISM services and prices-paid at multi-year highs) offset Waller ahead of today's jobs report where DB forecasts a +65k payrolls rebound with unemployment steady at 4.1%, while Japan's eighth straight monthly spending contraction sits ahead of a BoJ meeting leaning toward a 25bp hike.
briefs.brief_chain: Dovish Waller comments plus falling European natgas paused the bond selloff, therefore equities outperformed long-end bonds even as hawkish ISM/prices-paid data offset Waller ahead of today's jobs report where DB forecasts a +65k payrolls rebound with unemployment steady at 4.1%, while Japan's eighth straight monthly spending contraction sits ahead of a BoJ meeting leaning toward a 25bp hike.

distortions.what: Brief omits that renewed confidence in a September hike (before Waller) had been driven by Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, and omits the yen's four-big-figure two-day move.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — neither detail changes the hike-odds read (51% vs 63%), the equity/bond reaction, or the jobs-report setup the brief conveys.

briefs.source_chain: Front-end vol has collapsed since the Iran war while back-end vol stays elevated, producing a steepened term structure and a 23-day streak with no 1% SPX decline aided by the Citadel/Aschenbrenner deleveraging, therefore the calm resembles the 2024 streak but lacks that episode's rates tailwind (yields moving the other way now), so the note reads the still-elevated long-dated VIX premium as deferred rather than eliminated volatility that a future selloff would resolve.
briefs.brief_chain: Front-end vol has collapsed since the Iran war while back-end vol stays elevated, producing a steepened term structure and a 23-day streak with no 1% SPX decline aided by the Citadel/Aschenbrenner deleveraging, therefore the calm resembles the 2024 streak but lacks that episode's rates tailwind, so the still-elevated long-dated VIX premium implies deferred rather than eliminated volatility that a future selloff would resolve.
